publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Recording Media for Television
abstract: This paper concentrates on the benefits that disk based systems using digital compression can bring. News use of recording technology falls broadly into three areas: field acquisition and on-site editing; studio centre post-production and transmission; and library archiving. Each area requires different solutions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new approach to tape recording
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Recording Media for Television
abstract: New technologies have been developed to realise fully static multitrack scanners for high density magnetic recording: the recording head is an inductive multiplexed type, and the readout is magneto-optic, using a linear CCD for multitrack detection, and a dedicated transducer in contact with the tape. The signal processing associated with these components is digital and time-multiplexed because of the large number of channels. The particular features of this new technology allow one to overcome the limitations and to offer at least the densities and data rates of helicoidal recorders, with the mechanical simplicity and robustness of longitudinal drives.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: EBU user requirements for new DVTR formats
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Recording Media for Television
abstract: This paper reviews the activities of the European Broadcasting Union in the field of video recording, and reproduces Technical Statement D 73-1992 'EBU requirements for a new generation of digital television tape recorders for 625/50 television systems'. Some departures from an earlier document D36-1982 'EBU requirements concerning digital video recording equipment' are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Disk recording for real time post production applications
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Recording Media for Television
abstract: An overview of post requirements is given with a comparison of media bandwidths available.
